genZNote: H2S positive like Salmonella, but this one's just an opportunist crashing the gut-flora party.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human and animal GI tract; widely distributed in soil, water, and sewage
habitat.hostAssociation: Normal gut flora in some individuals; opportunistic pathogen
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Found in soil, water, food, and sewage

culture.colonyMorphology: Colorless to pink colonies, black-centered on XLD due to H2S production

identificationClues: Gram-negative motile rod, H2S positive — can resemble Salmonella on enteric media (black-centered colonies on XLD)
Late or variable lactose fermentation, citrate positive
Distinguished from Salmonella by additional biochemical testing and serology
Classic (though rare) cause of neonatal meningitis with a strong tendency toward brain abscess formation

diseases: Neonatal meningitis with a notably high rate of subsequent brain abscess (classic teaching association)
virulenceFactors: Ability to invade and persist in the neonatal CNS with high abscess formation potential
Can acquire AmpC beta-lactamases and other resistance mechanisms
clinicalImportance.transmission: Endogenous gut flora; nosocomial transmission in neonatal units
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: An uncommon but classic cause of neonatal meningitis, notable for one of the highest rates of brain abscess complication among causes of neonatal meningitis
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: H2S production means it can initially be mistaken for Salmonella on selective enteric media; motility, biochemical panel, and serology differentiate them

examFacts.importantDisease: UTI; classic (rare) cause of neonatal meningitis with brain abscess
examFacts.importantTest: H2S production on XLD/Hektoen agar (resembles Salmonella)
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: An H2S-producing Enterobacteriaceae classically linked to neonatal meningitis with an unusually high rate of brain abscess formation
